title: C# Questions & Answers - Recursion
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on recursion of C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What is Recursion in CSharp defined as?

options.text: Recursion is another form of class
Recursion is another process of defining a method that calls other methods repeatedly
Recursion is a process of defining a method that calls itself repeatedly
Recursion is a process of defining a method that calls other methods which in turn calls this method

questions.explanation: Recursion is the process of defining something in terms of itself. It allows us to define method that calls itself repeatedly until it meets some base case condition.

questions.question: Which of these will happen if the recursive method does not have a base case?

options.text: After 10000 executions program will be automatically stopped

questions.explanation: If a recursive method does not have a base case which is necessary to meet the end of condition then an infinite loop occurs which results in stackoverflow exception error.

questions.question: Which of these is not a correct statement?

options.text: A recursive method must have a base case
Recursion is always managed by C# Runtime environment
Recursive methods are faster that programmer written loop to call the function repeatedly using a stack

questions.explanation: Recursive methods are typically slower than an equivalent loop because of call overhead. Recursion uses the call stack (managed by the CLR), and a recursive method should have a base case.

questions.question: Which of these data types is used by the operating system to manage the Recursion in Csharp?
questions.explanation: The CLR uses the call stack to store return addresses and locals for each recursive invocation.
